agency_short: Rhode Island Department of Human Services (DHS)
admin_note: Rhode Island is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DHS administers directly through Regional Family Centers, with no county-level policy variation (Rhode Island's five counties have no independent county-government layer at all), structurally similar to this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, North Carolina, Ohio, New Jersey, Tennessee, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Louisiana, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kansas, New Mexico, and New Hampshire packs. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING: Rhode Island runs a TWO-TIER categorical-eligibility gross-income gate rather than a single flat BBCE percentage — 185% FPG for households without an elderly (60+) or disabled member, and a HIGHER 200% FPG threshold for households WITH an elderly/disabled member — this pack fetched DHS's own current (10/1/2025) SNAP Monthly Income Guidelines and cross-checked it directly against DHS's live Eligibility & How to Apply page, both agreeing precisely. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING, a genuine primary-source CONFIRMATION via the state's own general laws: Rhode Island fully opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban, codified directly in R.I. Gen. Laws § 40-6-8(d) (most recently amended 2025, opt-out clause itself untouched since at least 1997), which this pack fetched and quotes verbatim — 'No person shall be ineligible for food stamp benefits due solely to the restricted eligibility rules otherwise imposed by § 115(a)(2) of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 ... 21 U.S.C. § 862a(a)(2)'; this pack additionally confirmed the state's own 268-page SNAP regulation (218-RICR-20-00-1) contains NO drug-felony-conviction disqualification provision anywhere in its text, only the standard federal fleeing-felon and SNAP-trafficking penalty provisions, corroborating the statutory opt-out by absence. THIRD FLAGSHIP FINDING, a genuine minority-position structural departure worth flagging explicitly: Rhode Island's vehicle-resource exclusion is CAPPED at two (2) vehicles per household (one per adult member, but never more than two total) — 218-RICR-20-00-1 § 1.5.5(D)(1)(d)(AA) — a narrower rule than the uncapped 'one vehicle per adult household member, regardless of count' rule this roster's New Hampshire and several other states carry; this pack cross-checked this specific figure against independent secondary-source corroboration (WorkWORLD, SNAP Screener) which matched precisely. FOURTH FINDING: Rhode Island's Standard Utility Allowance is a SINGLE combined tier ($844/month, current FFY2026, up from $822) covering heating/cooling AND all other utilities (electricity, non-heat gas, water, sewer, trash, and one basic telephone line) — a simpler two-method utility-cost structure (SUA vs. a $26/month Standard Telephone Allowance for phone-only households not SUA-eligible) than this roster's New Hampshire, which carries a 4-tier utility structure split by type; see shelter-utility-deductions supplement. FIFTH FINDING: Rhode Island delayed its OBBBA ABAWD work-requirement rollout to March 1, 2026 for newly-affected ABAWDs — later than the federal November 1, 2025 effective date most other states in this roster implemented on — per DHS's own current (updated 1/7/2026) ABAWD FAQ; see abawd-work-requirement supplement. Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DHS Regional Family Center, the same caution this roster already carries for its other built states.
system: DHS administers SNAP directly and centrally through Regional Family Centers (no county offices with independent policy authority); applicants apply online through the Customer Portal (healthyrhode.ri.gov, part of the state's RIBridges integrated-eligibility system) or the HealthyRhode Mobile App, by phone through the DHS Call Center (1-855-MY-RIDHS / 1-855-697-4347), by mail or drop-off to P.O. Box 8709, Cranston, RI 02920-8787, or in person at a Regional Family Center. 'SNAP Connect' is DHS's separate on-demand phone-interview-scheduling initiative, not a distinct application portal — this pack flags this explicitly since a household could reasonably assume SNAP Connect is where they apply. Households consisting entirely of elderly (60+) or disabled members with no earned income are certified under the Elderly & Disabled Simplified Application Project (ESAP) for a 36-month certification period; migrant/seasonal farmworker households receive 24 months; all other households receive the standard 12-month certification period — Rhode Island's 12-month standard matches the norm most of this roster's other states use, in contrast to New Hampshire's unusually short 6-month standard. The RIBridges Customer Portal (healthyrhode.ri.gov) suffered a major ransomware data-breach in December 2024 (vendor Deloitte; Brain Cipher group claimed responsibility; ~650,000 Rhode Islanders' data potentially affected) that took the portal offline; DHS completed a phased public relaunch by early-to-mid 2025 and the State reached a $12 million settlement with Deloitte — this pack flags this as resolved historical context, not a current operative barrier, since the portal has been live and stable throughout this pack's own research window.

verification.method: dhs.ri.gov returned clean HTTP 200 to every direct curl attempt with a standard browser User-Agent — no WAF/bot-detection barrier this pack encountered, unlike this roster's New Hampshire pack. rules.sos.ri.gov (Rhode Island's official regulation host) is a JavaScript single-page application that returns a mostly-empty shell to a plain curl fetch; this pack resolved this by using WebFetch (which renders JavaScript) for the table-of-contents structure and, more importantly, by locating and directly curl-fetching dhs.ri.gov's own hosted copy of the full 268-page 218-RICR-20-00-1 regulation PDF (dhs.ri.gov/media/7796/download), which this pack ran through pdftotext -layout to extract full verbatim section text for categorical eligibility, resources, and deductions. This pack caught a genuine tooling trap in that PDF: it is Rhode Island's own AUGUST 2024 redlined rulemaking-amendment version, meaning several dollar figures inside it are shown as struck-through OLD values immediately followed by NEW values in a single garbled string (e.g. resource limits render as literal '$4,250500.00' meaning old-$4,250-struck-through/new-$4,500-inserted) — this pack did NOT take those redlined figures as current and instead cross-verified every dollar figure against DHS's own separately-fetched, dated FFY2026 SNAP Annual Cost of Living Adjustment PDF (effective October 1, 2025) and DHS's live Eligibility & How to Apply page, both confirming the CURRENT figures independently of the stale 2024 PDF's structural/procedural (non-dollar) text, which this pack does treat as still operative.
verification.gates: No access barrier at dhs.ri.gov itself — every direct curl attempt with a standard browser User-Agent returned a clean HTTP 200, including PDF downloads. The only friction this pack encountered was rules.sos.ri.gov's JavaScript-rendered regulation browser, which a plain curl fetch could not extract full section body text from; this pack resolved this entirely by using dhs.ri.gov's own hosted PDF of the same regulation instead, which a plain curl + pdftotext pipeline fetched cleanly. This pack also caught and explicitly did not rely on redlined/struck-through dollar figures inside that PDF (dated August 2024, reflecting an FFY2023-to-FFY2024 rulemaking amendment), instead cross-checking every current dollar figure against DHS's own separately-dated FFY2026 COLA PDF and live eligibility page. fna.usda.gov (the ABAWD waiver index) and webserver.rilegislature.gov (Rhode Island General Laws) both returned clean HTTP 200 to direct curl attempts; no barrier at either.
